deep.reconstruction:
Context: X is a space (or topos) with a global stratification indexed by a poset I. The closed pieces X_i satisfy, by the axioms recalled on the next page: X_i closed and locally finite, i<=j implies X_i in X_j, X is the union of the X_i, and X_i ∩ X_j is the union of the X_k with k<=i,j. The open strata are X_i^* = X_i minus the lower X_k. For each pair i<j with j an immediate successor of i, V_ij is a tubular neighbourhood of X_i^* in X_j, and V_ij^* is the corresponding deleted neighbourhood (the 'link' object). In the page's own notation the deleted neighbourhood is written V_ij^* = U_ij \ X_i^*, with the variable written U_ij, as transcribed. Diagram (17), on an earlier page not given here, has three types of solid-line arrows: V_ij^* -> V_ij (inclusion of the deleted neighbourhood), V_ij -> X_i^* (tubular retraction), and V_ij^* -> X_j^* (inclusion into the higher open stratum). These form a diagram of topoi of a shape \tilde I built from I.

Theorem ('Théorème de recollement des topos, 1ère version'): the topos of X is identified with the 2-limit of this diagram of topoi. Since the text later calls it a 'système inductif', this means a 2-colimit in the 2-category of topoi. The marginal proviso says that statements about X itself, rather than its topos, require X to be sober, i.e. determined by Top(X).

A deleted paragraph proposed proving the theorem only after replacing the abstract tubular neighbourhoods V_ij by genuine open neighbourhoods of X_i in X_j. In that case the claim reduces essentially to descent for an open cover: X_j = V ∪ X_j^*, with overlap the deleted neighbourhood. He abandoned this 'for lack of formal definitions of tubular neighbourhoods'. Instead he announces two things:
- a heuristic proof;
- first, a generalization that also expresses the 'canonical topoi' attached to the stratification as colimits of the \tilde I-indexed inductive system of 'elementary topoi'.

The next page (§4) starts this. It shows that the axioms are stable under base change X' -> X, and introduces chain-indexed objects X_{Δ_r}, X^*_{Δ_r} and \dot X_{Δ_r}, compatible with base change.

Modern reading: this is a dévissage or 'décollage' theorem. A stratified topos is reconstructed by gluing its strata along tubular neighbourhoods and links. For two strata this is Artin gluing / recollement: Sh(X) is the comma category of Sh(Z) and Sh(U) along i^*j_*. Here i^*j_* is computed through the oriented product (vanishing topos) Z ×←_X U, which plays the role of the deleted tubular neighbourhood. The general chain-indexed version anticipates the exodromy/décollage formalism.
errors: The identification cannot hold as a strict (pseudo) colimit if V_ij is a genuine open neighbourhood and the strata X_i^* are used in place of V_ij. Replacing a neighbourhood by the stratum via the retraction is only valid up to homotopy, or for homotopy-invariant (locally constant or constructible) sheaves, or if V_ij is defined abstractly (mapping cylinder, oriented product). For general sheaves one needs a lax colimit (Artin gluing with a 2-cell), not a plain 2-colimit. Grothendieck seems aware of this: he deletes the 'vrais voisinages' proof and calls the remaining argument heuristic.

Using only pairs with j an immediate successor of i is probably insufficient for deep strata. Compatibilities along chains i<j<k (iterated links) are needed, which is presumably why the next page passes to the chain-indexed X_{Δ_r}.
Recovering the space X itself (not just its topos) requires sobriety, as the margin notes. 'Limite' should be read as 2-colimit (limite inductive) in the 2-category of topoi.

ideas.what: Reconstruction of the topos of a stratified space as a 2-colimit of the topoi of open strata, tubular neighbourhoods and deleted neighbourhoods (diagram of type \tilde I)
ideas.modern_name: Décollage / exodromy reconstruction of stratified topoi; homotopy-link gluing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin gluing (SGA4); MacPherson, Treumann and Lurie (exit paths, Higher Algebra App. A); Barwick–Glasman–Haine, Exodromy (c. 2018–2020); Haine; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzipping)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 announces a dévissage of tame stratified structures into strata and tubular neighbourhoods, but no precise topos-theoretic theorem.

ideas.what: Proof strategy using genuine open neighbourhoods, reducing to descent for an open cover (abandoned)
ideas.modern_name: Descent for open covers / Mayer–Vietoris gluing of sheaf categories

ideas.what: Sober space determined by its topos
'Canonical topoi' attached to a stratification expressed through the inductive system of elementary topoi, with stability under base change (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Functorial décollage; stratified topoi indexed by chains in the poset (links X_{Δ_r})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Barwick–Glasman–Haine (decollages indexed by the subdivision of P)

missed.claim: Around 1981 Grothendieck formulated a 'recollement theorem for topoi': a stratified space's topos is the colimit of a diagram of strata, tubular neighbourhoods and links, indexed by a category \tilde I built from the stratification poset. He then generalized it to chain-indexed systems X_{Δ_r} of 'elementary topoi'. This is essentially the décollage picture of Barwick–Glasman–Haine's exodromy, where links are iterated oriented products indexed by chains in P, and of Lurie's exit-path reconstruction, some 35 years earlier, in topos language.
missed.quote: Alors X s'identifie au topos limite de ces topos ... en termes du système inductif de type \tilde I formé des topos élémentaires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and motivation for the exodromy/décollage program. Also a pointer that Grothendieck intended tubular neighbourhoods as topos-theoretic objects (cf. oriented products / vanishing topoi), which is how the modern theory defines links.

missed.claim: He notes the lack of a formal definition of tubular neighbourhoods in topos terms and gives only a heuristic proof. A rigorous definition of abstract tubular neighbourhoods making the strict gluing statement true is left open here.
missed.quote: Faute de disposer des définitions en forme pour les voisinages tubulaires ... Nous en donnons une démonstration heuristique ci-dessous
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Largely resolved in modern work (oriented fibre products, homotopy links, ∞-topoi), so of mainly historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear early formulation of a recollement/décollage theorem for stratified topoi via strata and tubular neighbourhoods, anticipating exodromy-style reconstruction. However, the idea is heuristic here, the gluing of strata is classical (Artin gluing, recollement), and the program is announced in Esquisse d'un programme.
transcription_corrections: Margin reads approximately: 'pourvu que en un sens précis, X soit sobre, i.e. déterminé par Top(X)...' ('sobre' underlined), not 'induit des strates'.
'(en haut p. bien)' is likely '(en trait plein)', i.e. the arrows drawn in solid lines in (17).
'2-topos' insertion is doubtful: the line reads 'X s'identifie au topos limite de ces topos', with corrections above; 'limite' is meant inductively (2-colimit).
The paragraph from 'Faute de disposer...' to 'V_ij^* = U_ij \ X_i^*' is struck through with diagonal lines in the image.
